domain_label: Turlock Food & Dining — Market, Demand & Saturation Economics
purpose: A method for sizing and reading the Turlock independent food-and-dining market: quantifying the demand drivers (resident base, CSU Stanislaus, the county ag/processing workforce, and the Assyrian/Portuguese/Mexican/Asian heritage communities), explaining why each format saturates at the count it does, accounting for cultural and weather seasonality, separating growing from declining formats, locating defensible white-space, comparing Turlock against its peer cities, and expressing all revenue and market-size figures strictly as labeled benchmark estimates (industry benchmark x observable size signal) rather than as stated facts.
assumptions: no per-business revenue dataset is supplied; every dollar figure is a labeled benchmark estimate, never an actual reported figure for any named business
the universe is the 40 verified Turlock independents in businesses.json (chains excluded), as of the 2026-06-30 snapshot
city/county/state figures (population, income, demographics, enrollment, permit fees) are cited public facts or explicitly labeled derivations

format-level revenue bands are published industry benchmarks (per seat / per sqft / per employee / per shop) scaled by an observable Turlock size signal, tagged estimate-not-actual with a confidence level and a confirmation path
Modesto (3x population, ~20 minutes north) is the regional dining anchor that caps Turlock's destination-dining ceiling
the single highest-leverage confirmation for the uncertain dollar figures is CDTFA / Turlock Finance restaurants-and-hotels sales-tax receipts
exclusions: per-format kitchen, equipment, staffing, and supplier-sourcing operations — covered by the supply-chain KB
per-format unit-economics, cost-structure and go/no-go business-model detail — covered by the business-models KB
any claim of an actual, reported, or audited dollar revenue for a named business
chain and franchise restaurants, which are outside the independents-only catalog
individual menu engineering, pricing tactics, or marketing execution for a specific operator

competency_questions.question: What are the demand drivers that generate Turlock's food-away spending pool, and how large is that resident pool as a labeled estimate?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DEMAND_DRIVERS names the resident base, CSU students, and ag/processing workforce; FOODAWAY_POOL gives the ~$99M (range $90M-$115M, medium confidence) resident pool as BLS spend x household count, tagged estimate-not-actual

competency_questions.question: How does Turlock's heritage density (Assyrian, Portuguese, Mexican, Asian) raise the format count above what population alone predicts?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HERITAGE_DEMAND ties each community share to the specific formats it anchors and explains the per-capita over-index on ethnic independents

competency_questions.question: How does the CSU Stanislaus student and commuter population shift demand toward particular formats and dayparts?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: STUDENT_COMMUTER_DEMAND quantifies the ~8,455-UG term-time lift and shows which formats (coffee, fast-casual, value) it disproportionately supports plus the academic-calendar swing

competency_questions.question: How much of the food-away pool do independents plausibly capture, and why is that capture share the weakest number in the analysis?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: INDEPENDENT_CAPTURE states the $35M-$50M (low-confidence) capture band, flags the outlet-share tension (20-30% of outlets vs 35-50% of dollars), and names the CDTFA confirmation

competency_questions.question: How is a per-format benchmark revenue band built so it is an honest estimate and never a stated fact for a named business?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BENCHMARK_REVENUE_BANDS states the benchmark x size-signal method, gives the per-format bands, and tags every band estimate-not-actual with confidence and a confirmation path

competency_questions.question: Why is the naive ~$1M-per-business average misleading, and what is the typical independent's benchmark band?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: POOL_MEAN_TRAP shows the ~$0.9M-$1.25M figure is a pool mean pulled up by a full-service/fine-dining right tail, and gives the $300k-$700k typical-independent cluster

competency_questions.question: Why does Turlock sustain roughly 40 independents — not 20, not 80 — and what four forces set that equilibrium?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SATURATION_EQUILIBRIUM names the four forces (demand floor, heritage depth, Modesto ceiling, format-level saturation) and ties the ~40 count to them

competency_questions.question: Which formats are at or near saturation and which retain headroom, by format-specific ceiling?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FORMAT_SATURATION_READS gives a per-format catalog count vs realistic ceiling and a saturated / balanced / room-to-grow read for each

competency_questions.question: How does Modesto's proximity cap Turlock's count and specifically its destination/fine-dining ceiling?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MODESTO_LEAKAGE explains the cross-shopping leakage to a 3x-larger anchor 20 minutes away and why it caps a fourth fine-dining room

competency_questions.question: How do cultural and weather seasonality concentrate demand in ways an annual revenue band averages away?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SEASONALITY names the format-specific peaks (panaderia Muertos/Reyes, Portuguese festas, mariscos Lent, ice cream summer, cafe academic calendar) and flags the working-capital risk

competency_questions.question: Which formats are growing on national tailwinds with local fit, and which are declining or under pressure?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: GROWTH_DECLINE separates growing formats (specialty/drive-thru coffee, fast-casual, food trucks) from declining ones (casual dining, undifferentiated coffee) with the national-trend basis

competency_questions.question: Where is the defensible white-space, and how is it ranked once both demand and the cost gate are considered?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: WHITESPACE_RANKING lists ranked openings (specialty coffee, South-Asian/Asian fast-casual, Portuguese sit-down, Assyrian grab-and-go, healthy bowls) each marked viable only after clearing the permit/license cost gate

competency_questions.question: How does Turlock compare to its peer cities (Modesto, Merced, Manteca, Tracy, Ceres) on per-capita independent density and format mix?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PEER_CITY_COMPARISON gives peer populations, the ~0.55 independents-per-1,000 read, and the structural contrasts (Ceres taqueria-heavy, Merced university+ag parallel, Tracy/Manteca chain-skewed)

competency_questions.question: How is a go/no-go market verdict reached for adding a format, what cost gate overrides a demand-true opening, and how are the market reads refreshed when the underlying figures change?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MARKET_GO_NOGO produces a verdict combining the saturation read, white-space rank, and permit/Type-47 cost gate (refusing demand-true but cost-gated additions), and MARKET_REVIEW_LOOP defines the refresh cadence and the material-change triggers (new CDTFA data, enrollment swing, plant open/close, demographic refresh) that re-run pool sizing and saturation

glossary.definition: The estimated total annual resident spending on food prepared outside the home, here ~$99M for Turlock = ~25,000 occupied households x the BLS 2024 national average of $3,945/household; a labeled estimate, not a measured figure.

The fraction of the food-away pool that locally owned independents (vs chains) collect; estimated at 35-50% but flagged low-confidence because it exceeds the ~20-30% independent outlet share, implying independents out-earn chains per outlet.

The honest revenue-estimation method used throughout: take a published per-seat / per-sqft / per-employee industry benchmark and scale it by an observable Turlock size signal (seat count, footprint, format), yielding a band tagged estimate-not-actual with a confidence level.

The distinction that the ~$0.9M-$1.25M figure (pool dollars / 40) is an arithmetic mean pulled up by a long full-service/fine-dining right tail, whereas the typical independent benchmarks $300k-$700k; conflating the two is the single most common misread.

The state in which the count of a format matches what local demand sustains given the anchoring community's size and Modesto's leakage; Turlock's ~40 total is read as such an equilibrium, not a deficit or a glut.

The capping effect of Modesto — three times Turlock's population, 20 minutes north — siphoning destination, national-concept, and fine-dining demand, the main force keeping Turlock's count from climbing past ~40.

Turlock carrying more ethnic independents per capita than population alone predicts, because California's largest Assyrian community (~20k), a ~7.3% Azorean/Portuguese base, a 46.1% Hispanic base, and a 5.6% Asian segment each anchor formats a generic 73k town would not.

An under-built format where both resident/student demand and operational feasibility permit entry; in Turlock the ranked openings are specialty/drive-thru coffee, South-Asian/Asian and Assyrian fast-casual, Portuguese sit-down, and healthy fast-casual — each only after the cost gate clears.

The permitting/licensing barrier that can override a demand-true opening: the ~$900 city + $69-$548 county + $114 license + mandatory-commissary stack for mobile, and the ABC Type 47 secondary-market wall (potentially six figures) for bar-forward concepts.

A per-capita density read: 40 independents / ~72,900 residents ~= 0.55 per 1,000, set against national foodservice bands of 1.7-2.8 per 1,000, implying independents are the ~20-30% locally owned slice of total outlets.

source_registry.description: labeled benchmark estimates and cited public facts for the Turlock independent food-and-dining market, grounded in the food_dining deep-dive (DEEPDIVE.md), its reconciled brief (reconciled.md), and the 40-business source dataset (businesses.json); demand sizing uses BLS food-away-from-home spend and ACS household counts, format revenue bands use published restaurant/cafe/bakery/food-truck benchmarks, and saturation/peer reads use census population and national restaurants-per-capita figures
source_registry.citation_or_locator: BLS Consumer Expenditure 2024 (food away from home, $3,945/household); ACS / California Demographics (Turlock ~72,900 pop, $82,995 median HH income, 46.1% Hispanic, 22.7% foreign-born); CSU Stanislaus enrollment (~8,455 UG, Fall 2024, Turlock Journal); KQED / Statistical Atlas (Assyrian ~20k, Portuguese ~7.3%); published cost/revenue benchmarks (Leverage Buying Group 2025, Toast, VantaInsights, CoffeeShopKeys, Sharpsheets, MenuTiger, Whipplewood CPAs, Lineup.ai); City Observatory / Toast restaurants-per-capita; CDTFA / Turlock Finance sales-tax categories (the confirmation source); food_dining DEEPDIVE.md, reconciled.md, businesses.json

nodes.definition: Catalog the three structural demand engines that feed Turlock's food-away spending: a ~72,900 resident base with a $82,995 median household income; the ~8,455-undergraduate (term-time ~9,400) CSU Stanislaus population that disproportionately lifts coffee, fast-casual and value demand; and a large county ag-and-food-processing workforce that drives early-morning, cash-friendly traffic. These three overlapping populations, not the resident count alone, set the demand the 40 independents share.

excluded: converting drivers into a dollar pool

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a population, enrollment, or workforce figure is refreshed

pros.claim: Naming three overlapping demand populations explains traffic a resident count alone cannot
pros.example: early-morning ag-shift and student coffee demand together fill dayparts a pure-residential read would miss

cons.claim: Overlapping populations risk double-counting spend if treated as independent pools
cons.example: a CSU student who also lives in Turlock counted twice inflates the apparent base

failure_modes: treating CSU enrollment as net-new spend rather than partly overlapping residents
ignoring the ag workforce because it does not appear in the resident census the same way
acceptance_tests: the three demand drivers are each named with a public-fact magnitude (resident pop, UG enrollment, ag/processing workforce presence) and tagged with their source confidence
revisit_triggers: a census or ACS demographic refresh
a CSU enrollment release
a major local plant opens, closes, or changes headcount

nodes.definition: Explain Turlock's defining demand feature: unusually deep heritage communities each anchor formats a generic 73k town would not carry. California's largest Assyrian community (~20,000, ~a quarter of town, the historic 'Little Urmia') anchors kebab houses and Mediterranean grills; a ~7.3% Azorean/Portuguese base sustained by ongoing immigration anchors Azorean bakeries; the 46.1% (overwhelmingly Mexican-origin) Hispanic base anchors taquerias, panaderias, mariscos and sit-down Mexican; and a 5.6% Asian/South-Asian segment supports pan-Asian concepts. This heritage density is why Turlock over-indexes per capita on ethnic independents.

included: Assyrian, Portuguese, Mexican, Asian community shares
excluded: the dollar size of each community's spend

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a heritage-community share or migration trend changes

pros.claim: Mapping community to format explains a count national density models under-predict
pros.example: three mariscos and three Assyrian rooms make sense only against the Mexican and ~20k Assyrian anchors

cons.claim: Ancestry share is a crude proxy for spend, since communities differ in dining frequency and price sensitivity
cons.example: a large but price-sensitive Mexican base supports many low-ticket formats but caps their revenue

failure_modes: assuming ancestry share converts linearly to format revenue
ignoring that heritage demand also draws non-community diners (Assyrian and mariscos cross over)
acceptance_tests: each of the four heritage communities is tied to at least one anchored format with its cited population share, and the per-capita over-index is stated explicitly
revisit_triggers: an ancestry/demographic data refresh
a heritage community grows or contracts via migration
a heritage-anchored format opens or closes

nodes.definition: Isolate how the CSU Stanislaus student body (~8,455 undergraduates Fall 2024, rebounding but not booming post-COVID) and the commuter flow reshape demand by format and daypart. Term-time students disproportionately lift specialty coffee, fast-casual, value and late-ish dayparts, while creating a strong academic-calendar swing — demand falls in summer and over breaks. This segment is the primary reason coffee and fast-casual retain headroom against national café density even though population alone looks fully served.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a CSU enrollment or commuter-pattern figure changes

pros.claim: Isolating student demand explains coffee/fast-casual headroom a resident-only read would deny
pros.example: TaZa's signature-drink, experiential positioning is built for the student segment, not the general resident

cons.claim: Student demand is calendar-fragile, so formats over-built on it face summer revenue holes
cons.example: a campus-adjacent café that empties between spring and fall terms

failure_modes: treating peak-term student traffic as year-round baseline
ignoring that enrollment is rebounding, not booming, so the lift is bounded
acceptance_tests: the student lift is tied to specific formats (coffee, fast-casual, value) with the ~8,455-UG figure and the academic-calendar swing is named as a seasonality factor
revisit_triggers: a CSU enrollment release moves the figure materially
a campus-housing or commuter-pattern change shifts daypart demand

nodes.definition: Size the resident food-away spending pool as a labeled estimate: ~25,000 occupied Turlock households x the BLS 2024 national average household spend on food away from home ($3,945) yields ~$99M/year (range $90M-$115M, medium confidence). This is the demand ceiling the whole market shares, explicitly an estimate, not a measured figure; its single best confirmation is CDTFA / Turlock Finance restaurants-and-hotels sales-tax receipts. Student and ag-workforce spend partly overlaps and partly adds to this resident pool rather than stacking cleanly on top of it.

excluded: the independent capture share (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a BLS spend figure, household count, or CDTFA receipt set is refreshed

pros.claim: A transparent BLS-x-household method gives a defensible pool ceiling without quoting any business
pros.example: stating ~$99M as 25,000 households x $3,945 lets a reader audit the estimate end to end

cons.claim: A national per-household average understates or overstates a town with atypical income and dining habits
cons.example: Turlock's above-US median income could push true spend above the national-average band

failure_modes: presenting the ~$99M as a measured figure rather than an estimate
stacking student and ag spend fully on top of the resident pool and double-counting
acceptance_tests: the pool is stated as ~$99M (range $90M-$115M) with the explicit BLS-spend x household-count derivation, a confidence level, and the CDTFA confirmation path, tagged estimate-not-actual
revisit_triggers: a new BLS food-away spend release
an ACS household-count refresh
CDTFA sales-tax receipts become available

nodes.definition: Estimate what fraction of the ~$99M pool independents (vs chains) capture, and flag it as the analysis's weakest number. The planning band is $35M-$50M/year (low confidence), the ethnic, owner-operated and downtown formats where chains do not compete. The tension: independents are only ~20-30% of total outlets, so a 35-50% dollar share implies they out-earn chains per outlet — plausible for full-service/ethnic destinations but unverified. If true capture is nearer the outlet share, the pool falls to ~$25M-$30M. CDTFA split by independent vs chain is the confirmation.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: CDTFA independent-vs-chain split or outlet count changes

pros.claim: Explicitly flagging capture as the weakest link prevents a false-precision market size
pros.example: marking 35-50% low-confidence stops a reader treating ~$42M independent spend as solid

cons.claim: A wide flagged band limits how much downstream planning can lean on the market size
cons.example: a $35M-$50M-or-maybe-$25M-$30M range is too wide to set a precise entry target on

failure_modes: upgrading the 35-50% planning assumption to a stated fact
ignoring the implication that 20-30% of outlets earning 35-50% of dollars needs verification
acceptance_tests: the capture share is stated as $35M-$50M low-confidence, the outlet-share-vs-dollar-share tension is named, and the ~$25M-$30M downside and CDTFA confirmation are both given
revisit_triggers: CDTFA splits receipts by independent vs chain
the independent outlet count materially changes

nodes.definition: Build the per-format revenue bands that are the primary, most defensible revenue view, every one a labeled estimate (published benchmark x observable Turlock size signal), never an actual figure for a named business. Representative bands: full-service ethnic/American sit-down $600k-$1.2M; contemporary American/fine dining $0.9M-$1.5M expected Turlock case; mariscos $500k-$1M; taqueria $300k-$720k; taco/food truck $250k-$490k (avg ~$346k); cafe $350k-$650k (median ~$500k); bakery-cafe $300k-$600k; panaderia $200k-$450k; Portuguese bakery $150k-$400k; gastropub/wine bar $600k-$1.3M; ice cream $250k-$500k; pan-Asian $400k-$800k. Each pairs revenue with its cost/margin reality so high gross is never read as high net.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a benchmark source or measured size signal changes

pros.claim: Per-format bands anchored to published benchmarks give a planning estimate without quoting any operator
pros.example: a cafe band of $350k-$650k from coffee-shop median revenue x footprint is auditable and business-agnostic

cons.claim: Bands rest on national benchmarks and unobserved size signals, so any single business can sit far outside its band
cons.example: a high-turn downtown cafe could exceed the $650k top while a small one falls below the floor

failure_modes: attaching a band to a named business as if it were that business's revenue
dropping the cost/margin pairing so a high-gross format reads as high-profit
acceptance_tests: each major format has a low/median/high band derived as benchmark x a stated size signal, tagged estimate-not-actual with a confidence and confirmation path, and paired with its cost/margin caveat
revisit_triggers: a published benchmark source updates
an observable size signal (seats, sqft, format mix) is measured for a format
CDTFA distribution data lands

nodes.definition: Correct the single most common misread: the naive '$35M-$50M / 40 ~= $0.9M-$1.25M per business' is a pool arithmetic mean, not a typical business. It is pulled up by a long right tail of full-service / fine-dining rooms and high-turn cafés, and is further inflated if the independent capture share is overstated. The typical Turlock independent benchmarks $300k-$700k (per the per-format bands). The ~$1M average should be read as a pool-average ceiling-of-plausibility at low confidence, with the per-format bands the primary view; CDTFA sales-tax distribution by outlet would resolve it.

pros.claim: Naming the pool-mean trap stops a reader concluding the average Turlock independent grosses ~$1M
pros.example: showing the mean sits above every non-full-service band exposes it as tail-driven

cons.claim: Emphasizing the correction can make the directional pool sanity-check seem worthless when it still has value
cons.example: discarding the average entirely loses a useful count-vs-demand consistency check

failure_modes: quoting ~$1M as the typical business
presenting a single point estimate instead of the $300k-$700k typical band
acceptance_tests: the ~$0.9M-$1.25M figure is labeled a pool mean (low confidence), its right-tail cause is stated, and the $300k-$700k typical-independent band is given as the primary read
revisit_triggers: CDTFA outlet-level distribution becomes available
the capture share or per-format bands are revised

nodes.definition: Explain why Turlock sustains roughly 40 independents — not 20, not 80 — as an equilibrium set by four forces: (1) a demand floor (~73k residents + ~8,500 students + an ag/processing workforce generating the ~$99M pool, of which independents capture $35M-$50M); (2) heritage depth that raises the count above what population predicts; (3) the Modesto ceiling that leaks destination demand and caps the climb; and (4) format-level saturation where the most price-sensitive (Mexican) or most cross-shopped (fine dining) formats hit their ceiling first. Forty is where each heritage niche and downtown slot is filled but no second or third of most concepts can be added without cannibalization.

excluded: the Modesto mechanism detail (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: one of the four equilibrium forces shifts

pros.claim: Framing 40 as an equilibrium of four forces resists both over-building and under-building conclusions
pros.example: it explains why neither a deficit nor a glut is the right read of the count

cons.claim: An equilibrium framing can imply false stability when trends (enrollment, casual-dining pressure) are moving
cons.example: treating 40 as fixed when specialty coffee growth could lift the sustainable count

failure_modes: reading the count as a deficit and recommending broad expansion
ignoring that the equilibrium drifts as the four forces change
acceptance_tests: all four forces are named and each is tied to the ~40-count outcome, with the cannibalization ceiling stated
revisit_triggers: one of the four forces shifts materially (pool size, heritage demand, Modesto draw, or a format's saturation)
the independent count moves away from ~40

nodes.definition: Give the per-format saturation read by setting the catalog count against a realistic ceiling for a ~73k town: cafe/coffeehouse 5 (+3 bakery-cafe straddle) vs 8-12, room to grow; taqueria+taco truck 3+3 vs 5-7, at/near saturation (sit-down) with trucks expandable; mariscos 3 vs 2-4, at saturation/over-indexed; sit-down Mexican 3 vs 3-4, saturated; panaderia 2 vs 2-4, slight room; Assyrian/Mediterranean 3 vs 3-5, well-matched; Portuguese bakery 1 vs 1-2, under-served; Italian/pizzeria 4 vs 4-6, balanced; fine dining 3 vs 3-5, at ceiling; gastropub/wine bar 3 vs 3-4, balanced; ice cream 2 vs 2-4, slight room; pan-Asian 1 vs 2-3, under-served.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a format's count or anchoring demand changes

pros.claim: A count-vs-ceiling table makes each format's headroom or saturation legible at a glance
pros.example: cafe 5 vs 8-12 reads as room while mariscos 3 vs 2-4 reads as over-indexed

cons.claim: Format ceilings are themselves estimates, so a saturated/room read can flip if the ceiling is mis-set
cons.example: a 'slight room' panaderia read reverses if Hispanic spend is lower than assumed

failure_modes: reading a primary-category count as the full picture when secondary-format straddles shift it
treating an estimated ceiling as a hard cap
acceptance_tests: each major format has a catalog count, a realistic ceiling range, and a saturated/balanced/room-to-grow read consistent with the equilibrium forces
revisit_triggers: a format opens or closes in the catalog
a demographic shift changes a format's anchoring community
Modesto leakage for a format is measured

nodes.definition: Model the Modesto ceiling: Modesto (~218,000, three times Turlock's population, ~20 minutes north) is the regional dining anchor, and destination dining, national concepts and big-box variety leak there. This cross-shopping is the main force keeping Turlock's count from climbing past ~40 and the specific reason a fourth fine-dining room is not advisable — Turlock's fine-dining rooms sit in the lower half of their revenue band because Modesto caps destination demand. The leakage is an estimate of behavior, not a measured figure; a Turlock-vs-Modesto cross-shop study would confirm it.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: Modesto cross-shop behavior or its dining scene changes

pros.claim: Naming Modesto leakage explains the fine-dining ceiling that demand math alone cannot
pros.example: a fourth romantic-destination room would split demand that already leaks to Modesto's larger scene

cons.claim: Leakage is inferred from proximity and scale, not measured, so its magnitude is uncertain
cons.example: without a cross-shop study the exact share of Turlock destination spend going to Modesto is unknown

failure_modes: treating the leakage estimate as a measured figure
applying the fine-dining ceiling logic to formats Modesto does not actually draw (heritage independents)
acceptance_tests: the Modesto anchor is quantified by population ratio and travel time, tied to the fine-dining ceiling, and flagged as an estimate of cross-shopping behavior with its confirmation path
revisit_triggers: a Turlock-vs-Modesto cross-shop leakage study is done
Modesto's dining scene expands or contracts materially
a new fine-dining room opens in Turlock

nodes.definition: Account for the demand peaks an annual revenue band averages away, which are a working-capital risk not visible in a flat band. Cultural: panaderia peaks at Dia de los Muertos and Dia de Reyes; Portuguese/Azorean bakery is festa-concentrated (the most seasonal format in the set); mariscos spikes during Lent. Weather: ice cream concentrates revenue in ~5-6 warm months with idle-winter fixed-cost pressure. Academic: cafés track the CSU calendar and dip in summer/breaks. An operator who reads only the annual band will mis-plan cash flow through the troughs.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a seasonal peak's timing or magnitude is observed to change

pros.claim: Surfacing format-specific peaks turns a flat annual band into an actionable cash-flow profile
pros.example: a Portuguese bakery's festa-season order book is its volume engine, invisible in an annual average

cons.claim: Seasonality detail is hard to quantify without operator data, so peaks are directional not sized
cons.example: knowing mariscos spikes at Lent does not say by how much without sales records

failure_modes: averaging a festa- or summer-concentrated business into a flat band and mis-sizing working capital
ignoring that the academic-calendar dip compounds with summer for campus-adjacent cafés
acceptance_tests: each seasonal format is tied to its specific peak (cultural, weather, or academic) and the working-capital/idle-cost risk is named explicitly
revisit_triggers: a calendar shift (festa schedule, academic calendar) changes a peak
operator sales data quantifies a peak's magnitude

nodes.definition: Separate growing formats from declining ones using national trends overlaid on local fit. Growing: specialty/drive-thru coffee (specialty-beverage concepts projected to post large sales gains; the clearest local growth lane given student+commuter demand); fast-casual/limited-service (~2% real growth, outpacing the industry); food trucks (~10.9% popularity CAGR, low capital). Mature/stable not growing: mariscos (culturally vibrant locally but US seafood menu penetration fell in 2024). Declining/under pressure: casual dining (among the weakest national segments; only ~34% of casual-dining companies posted positive same-store sales mid-2024) and legacy/undifferentiated coffee (squeezed even as specialty grows).

excluded: white-space ranking and cost gate (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a national trend release or local outlet change shifts a trajectory

pros.claim: Overlaying national trajectory on local fit distinguishes a saturated-but-growing lane from a saturated-and-declining one
pros.example: coffee is near-saturated by count yet growing in the specialty/drive-thru sub-format

cons.claim: National trends may not transfer cleanly to a heritage-heavy Valley town
cons.example: casual-dining national weakness understates durable local heritage sit-downs

failure_modes: treating mariscos as a growth lane because it is culturally vibrant when the segment is mature
applying national casual-dining decline to heritage formats it does not describe
acceptance_tests: growing, mature, and declining formats are each named with their national-trend basis and their Turlock local-fit qualifier
revisit_triggers: a new national restaurant-trend release
a local format visibly gains or loses outlets against the trend

nodes.definition: Locate and rank the defensible white-space — formats where both demand and operations permit entry — and mark each viable only after the cost gate clears. Ranked: (1) specialty/drive-thru coffee (strongest national growth + CSU/commuter demand, moderate capex, county permit only — best risk-adjusted opportunity); (2) South-Asian/Asian fast-casual (under-built vs 5.6% Asian + student base; watch multi-cuisine SKU/waste cost); (3) Portuguese/Azorean sit-down or expanded bakery-café (genuine heritage white space at 7.3%, but festa seasonality is a cash-flow risk); (4) Assyrian fast-casual/grab-and-go (captures lunch/student traffic sit-downs miss); (5) healthy/fast-casual bowls & wellness beverages (nearly absent, CSU-skewed); (6) dessert/late-night (thin for a college town).

excluded: the per-decision go/no-go verdict (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a white-space opening is entered or its demand/cost gate changes

pros.claim: Ranking white-space by demand and feasibility together prevents recommending a demand-true but un-enterable format
pros.example: specialty drive-thru coffee ranks first because growth, local demand, and a county-permit-only path all align

cons.claim: A ranked list can read as a recommendation to enter when each opening still needs an operator's own feasibility check
cons.example: South-Asian fast-casual ranks high but its SKU/waste risk could sink a specific operator

failure_modes: listing white-space on demand alone without the cost gate, so a bar concept looks open when Type 47 walls it
ranking a heritage opening without flagging its seasonality cash-flow risk
acceptance_tests: at least five white-space openings are ranked, each with its demand basis and an explicit cost-gate (permit/Type 47/commissary) qualifier
revisit_triggers: a white-space format is entered locally
a demographic or trend shift changes an opening's demand
a permit/license fee or availability changes the cost gate

nodes.definition: Define the entry cost gate that can override a demand-true opening, the barrier the demand view alone misses. Bar-forward concepts face the ABC Type 47 (full liquor) secondary-market license wall — potentially $100k-$200k in tight counties on top of $6,275-$16,560 application and $925-$1,450 annual fees. Mobile concepts face a stacked $900 city mobile permit + $69-$548 county mobile permit + $114 city business license + a mandatory commissary. These are cited public fees. The market read must treat 'low-capital truck' and 'easy white space' as demand-true but cost-gated: the binding constraint is often permitting, not ingredient cost.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a permit, license, or commissary fee or availability changes

pros.claim: Foregrounding the cost gate prevents a demand-true opening from being read as actually enterable
pros.example: a wine bar looks like balanced white space until the six-figure Type 47 wall is priced in

cons.claim: License/permit costs vary and the secondary-market wall is county-specific, so the figure is a range not a fixed cost
cons.example: the Type 47 secondary-market price swings widely with county license availability

failure_modes: recommending a bar-forward or mobile opening without pricing the gate
treating the commissary requirement as optional for trucks
acceptance_tests: the Type 47 wall and the mobile permit+commissary stack are each stated with their cited public fee figures and applied as an override on the relevant white-space openings
revisit_triggers: a city/county/ABC fee schedule changes
Type 47 secondary-market license availability shifts in the county

nodes.definition: Benchmark Turlock against peer cities on per-capita independent density and format mix. Populations (2024 est., cited): Modesto ~218,000, Tracy ~96,966, Merced ~91,953, Manteca ~83,500, Turlock ~72,900, Ceres ~49,342. At ~72,900 residents, 40 independents = ~0.55 per 1,000; total foodservice at the 1.7-2.8/1,000 national bands would be ~130-200 outlets, so independents are the ~20-30% locally owned slice — a healthy, not saturated, share. Modesto is the anchor that pulls cross-shopping; Ceres (65% Hispanic) is taqueria-heavy and lacks Turlock's Assyrian/fine-dining breadth; Tracy/Manteca are chain-skewed Bay-Area-spillover commuter cities; Merced parallels Turlock's university+ag structure with a younger, lower-income student base.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a peer-city population or foodservice-mix figure changes

pros.claim: Per-capita and structural peer contrasts place Turlock's count in regional context rather than in isolation
pros.example: ~0.55 independents per 1,000 against the national band shows the 40 is a healthy locally owned share

cons.claim: Peer cities differ in demographics and Bay-Area proximity, so density comparison alone can mislead
cons.example: Tracy's chain-skew reflects commuter spillover, not a fairer comparison of independent depth

failure_modes: comparing raw independent counts without normalizing per capita
ignoring that Merced's younger/lower-income student base differs from CSU Stanislaus despite the shared university+ag structure
acceptance_tests: peer populations are cited, the ~0.55-per-1,000 and ~20-30% locally owned share are derived, and at least three peers (Modesto, Ceres, Merced or Tracy/Manteca) are contrasted structurally
revisit_triggers: a peer-city population refresh
a peer's foodservice mix shifts (new development, a university change)
a national restaurants-per-capita update

nodes.definition: Read the specific way Turlock differs from peers: it over-indexes per capita on ethnic independents because of heritage density Modesto and the commuter cities lack. Modesto has more independents in absolute terms but Turlock carries more Assyrian, Portuguese and Mexican formats per resident; Ceres leans Mexican/taqueria but lacks Assyrian and fine-dining breadth; Tracy/Manteca skew toward newer chain and fast-casual with thin deep-heritage scenes. This over-index is the structural reason Turlock supports format depth (mariscos, Assyrian grills, Azorean bakeries) that population-only or national-density models under-predict for a 73k town.

included: the per-capita ethnic over-index vs peers

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a heritage share or peer ethnic-scene comparison changes

pros.claim: Isolating the ethnic over-index explains format depth a national-density model under-predicts
pros.example: three mariscos and three Assyrian rooms in a 73k town read as deficit only until heritage over-index is applied

cons.claim: Over-indexing on heritage formats concentrates risk in community-specific demand
cons.example: an Azorean bakery depends on a 7.3% base whose festa-driven demand is narrow and seasonal

failure_modes: attributing Turlock's depth to size rather than heritage
assuming the over-index transfers to peers without their community density
acceptance_tests: the per-capita ethnic over-index is stated relative to at least two peers and tied to the specific heritage formats it supports
revisit_triggers: a heritage community share changes
a peer city's ethnic-independent scene grows
a demographic refresh alters the comparison

nodes.definition: Enforce the binding honesty discipline across every dollar figure: per-business revenue is not public, so no dollar figure is ever stated as an actual reported figure for a named business. Every format dollar band is a labeled benchmark estimate (published benchmark x observable size signal) tagged estimate-not-actual with a confidence level and a confirmation path; every high-gross band is paired with its thin-net-margin caveat; city/county/state figures are cited public facts or labeled derivations; supplier-to-named-business links are representative inference unless a cited source states otherwise. This guardrail governs how all the sizing and band nodes may be expressed.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a new dollar figure is introduced or an actual datum becomes available

pros.claim: A single explicit guardrail keeps every downstream number honest and auditable
pros.example: tagging the ~$99M pool and every format band estimate-not-actual prevents any figure being read as audited

cons.claim: Heavy labeling can make the analysis read as hedged and lower its perceived usefulness
cons.example: a reader wanting a single revenue number is frustrated by a band tagged low-confidence

failure_modes: letting a format band attach to a named business as that business's revenue
stating a city/county figure without a source or a derivation label
acceptance_tests: every dollar figure in any node is a labeled estimate or a cited public fact, no named-business actual revenue appears, and each high-gross band carries its thin-net caveat
revisit_triggers: a new node introduces a dollar figure
a public-fact source is added or updated
an actual revenue datum (e.g., CDTFA) becomes available to replace an estimate

nodes.definition: Produce the market go/no-go verdict for adding a given format, composing the saturation read, the white-space rank, the growth/decline trajectory, and the cost gate into one decision. The merged rule: do not add a sixth taqueria, a fourth mariscos, or a fourth fine-dining room (all saturated/capped); the defensible headroom is specialty/drive-thru coffee, South-Asian/Asian and Assyrian fast-casual, Portuguese sit-down, and healthy fast-casual — each viable only after clearing the county-permit (and, for bar concepts, Type 47) cost gate. A demand-true opening that fails the cost gate is a no-go until the gate clears.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a saturation, trajectory, or cost-gate input to the verdict changes

pros.claim: Composing all reads into one verdict gives an actionable add/avoid call instead of scattered signals
pros.example: the verdict says no to a fourth mariscos but yes to drive-thru coffee once the county permit is cleared

cons.claim: A single verdict can over-simplify a format whose demand and cost gate point opposite ways
cons.example: an Assyrian grab-and-go has demand headroom yet still needs a feasibility pass before a clean yes

failure_modes: issuing a yes on demand headroom while ignoring an unmet cost gate
recommending a saturated format because its heritage anchor looks durable
acceptance_tests: the verdict for a proposed format combines its saturation read, white-space rank, trajectory, and cost-gate status, and refuses any demand-true but cost-gated addition
revisit_triggers: a saturation read, trajectory, or cost gate feeding the verdict changes
a previously gated opening clears its cost gate

nodes.definition: Define the loop that keeps the market reads current. A fixed refresh cadence (e.g., re-run on each major data release) plus material-change triggers — new CDTFA / Turlock Finance sales-tax receipts (which collapse pool size, capture share, and per-business distribution at once), a CSU enrollment swing, a major local plant opening or closing, a census/ACS demographic refresh, a national restaurant-trend release, or a permit/license fee change — that send the analysis back through FOODAWAY_POOL and the saturation reads. Without this loop the 2026-06-30 snapshot silently goes stale as enrollment rebounds, casual dining stays pressured, and specialty coffee grows.

included: re-entry into pool sizing and saturation

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a material-change trigger fires or the cadence is tuned

pros.claim: A trigger list with the CDTFA confirmation keeps the lowest-confidence numbers on a path to resolution
pros.example: the arrival of sales-tax receipts fires the loop and replaces three estimates with measured figures at once

cons.claim: Too-frequent refresh churns the reads without new signal, since most inputs update only annually
cons.example: re-sizing the pool monthly when BLS spend and ACS counts move only yearly wastes effort

failure_modes: no cadence set so the snapshot ages silently past its trend assumptions
ignoring a fired trigger (new CDTFA data) and continuing on stale estimates
acceptance_tests: a refresh cadence and an explicit material-change trigger list exist, each routing back to FOODAWAY_POOL and the saturation reads, with CDTFA named as the highest-leverage trigger
revisit_triggers: a material-change trigger fires
the cadence proves too frequent or too sparse for how the inputs actually update

edges.why_related: heritage anchoring is a refinement of the broad demand-driver base into community-specific demand
the student/commuter daypart read isolates one of the three demand drivers in detail
the resident pool is sized from the resident base named among the demand drivers
the independent capture band is a fraction of the resident pool just sized
per-format bands are cross-checked against the total pool they must sum within
which formats exist to band, and their anchoring demand, comes from the heritage map
the misleading per-business average is the capture pool divided by the business count
the typical-business $300k-$700k cluster that corrects the average is read off the per-format bands
the demand-floor force in the equilibrium uses the independent-capturable dollar pool
the heritage-depth force that raises the count above population prediction comes from the heritage map
per-format reads decompose the overall equilibrium into format-by-format count-vs-ceiling calls
the Modesto-ceiling force in the equilibrium is detailed in the leakage node
Modesto leakage causally lowers the realistic ceiling for the destination/fine-dining formats
the cultural peaks (Muertos/Reyes, festas, Lent) follow directly from the heritage communities
the academic-calendar demand swing is a seasonality factor inherited from the student demand node
the trajectory overlay reads the saturated/room status of each format before judging growth or decline
the coffee/fast-casual growth lanes depend on the student/commuter demand that feeds them
white-space is the under-served end of the per-format saturation reads
growing formats with local fit are ranked highest in the white-space order
the cost gate is applied as an override on each ranked white-space opening
demand ranks an opening attractive while the permit/license cost can make it un-enterable, pulling opposite ways
edges.resolution_rule: a demand-true opening is a no-go until its cost gate (county permit + commissary for mobile, Type 47 for bar-forward) is cleared; demand never overrides an unmet cost gate

edges.why_related: the per-capita density read needs the Turlock resident base from the demand drivers
the format-mix contrasts against peers build on Turlock's own per-format reads
the per-capita ethnic over-index is the comparative expression of the heritage map
the over-index is measured against the peer cities the comparison node establishes
the guardrail governs how the per-format bands may be expressed and labeled
the guardrail enforces the estimate-not-actual labeling on the capture and pool figures
the pool-mean correction is itself an instance of the honesty discipline and reinforces it
summing the per-format bands across 40 businesses tensions against the top-down capture pool when capture is overstated
edges.resolution_rule: treat the per-format bands as the primary view and the capture-derived average as a low-confidence pool ceiling; reconcile only against CDTFA outlet-level data

edges.why_related: the go/no-go verdict consumes the per-format saturation read
the verdict elevates the highest-ranked white-space openings as candidate yeses
the verdict applies the cost gate as the override that can turn a demand-true yes into a no
the verdict weighs each format's growth or decline trajectory in the add/avoid call
the verdict must express any revenue rationale as a labeled estimate under the guardrail
the review loop watches the inputs to the verdict and re-triggers it when they change
a new BLS/ACS/CDTFA release sends the analysis back to re-size the pool
a plant open/close or enrollment swing re-runs the saturation reads
annual bands must be read with the seasonality caveat so a festa- or summer-concentrated format is not mis-planned on a flat average
the verdict must not lean on the ~$1M pool-mean average and instead use the typical-business band

conflict_axes.name: demand_headroom_vs_cost_gate
conflict_axes.description: A format can be demand-true white space yet be walled off by permitting or liquor-license cost, so the demand and feasibility views point opposite ways.
poles: block on the unmet cost gate
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: treat a demand-true opening as a no-go until its cost gate clears; demand never overrides permitting

conflict_axes.name: pool_average_vs_typical_business
conflict_axes.description: The top-down pool mean (~$1M/business) and the bottom-up per-format bands ($300k-$700k typical) cannot both describe a typical business.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the per-format band is the primary view; the pool mean is a low-confidence ceiling pulled up by a right tail

conflict_axes.name: outlet_share_vs_dollar_share
conflict_axes.description: Independents are ~20-30% of outlets but assumed to capture 35-50% of dollars, implying per-outlet out-earning that is unverified.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: retain 35-50% only as a low-confidence planning band; the ~$25M-$30M downside strengthens internal consistency until CDTFA confirms

conflict_axes.name: heritage_depth_vs_modesto_ceiling
conflict_axes.description: Heritage demand pushes the format count above population prediction while Modesto's gravity pulls destination demand away and caps it.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: heritage raises the ceiling for ethnic/owner-operated formats; Modesto caps destination/fine-dining formats; apply each to the formats it governs

conflict_axes.name: national_trend_vs_local_heritage_durability
conflict_axes.description: National decline signals (casual dining, undifferentiated coffee) can mislabel durable local heritage formats that the trend does not describe.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: apply national trends to undifferentiated formats; discount them for heritage-anchored formats with durable community demand

conflict_axes.name: annual_band_vs_seasonal_concentration
conflict_axes.description: A flat annual revenue band averages away the festa/summer/Lent/Muertos peaks that drive working-capital risk.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: always pair the annual band with the format's seasonal peak profile before any cash-flow read

conflict_axes.name: per_capita_density_vs_structural_mix
conflict_axes.description: Comparing Turlock to peers on raw per-capita density can mislead when peers differ structurally (chain-skew, demographics, Bay-Area proximity).
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: normalize per capita first, then qualify with the structural contrast (heritage depth, chain-skew) before drawing a conclusion

conflict_axes.name: estimate_labeling_vs_decisiveness
conflict_axes.description: Rigorous estimate-not-actual labeling protects honesty but can make the analysis read as too hedged to act on.
poles: label every figure as an estimate
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: label every figure but pair it with a confidence and a confirmation path so the read stays actionable without overclaiming

conflict_axes.name: snapshot_stability_vs_trend_drift
conflict_axes.description: The ~40 equilibrium reads as stable, but rebounding enrollment, casual-dining pressure, and specialty-coffee growth are moving the underlying forces.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: hold the snapshot as a dated baseline but let the review loop, not assumption, decide when drift has moved the equilibrium

edge_cases.description: A reader treats the ~$0.9M-$1.25M pool average as a typical business's revenue
edge_cases.trigger: the pool dollars are divided by 40 and quoted as a per-business figure
edge_cases.mitigation: label the average a low-confidence pool mean and present the $300k-$700k typical-independent band as the primary read

edge_cases.description: A format band is attached to a named business as if it were that business's actual revenue
edge_cases.trigger: a per-format estimate is quoted next to a specific operator's name
edge_cases.mitigation: keep every band format-level and estimate-not-actual; never bind a dollar figure to a named business as fact

edge_cases.description: Independent capture is assumed at 35-50% with no flag, inflating the market size
edge_cases.trigger: the capture band is used as a solid figure in downstream sizing
edge_cases.mitigation: mark capture low-confidence, carry the ~$25M-$30M downside, and route to CDTFA for confirmation

edge_cases.description: A bar-forward white-space opening is recommended without pricing the Type 47 wall
edge_cases.trigger: a wine bar or tap house is judged on demand headroom alone
edge_cases.mitigation: apply the Type 47 secondary-market wall as an override before any bar-forward yes

edge_cases.description: A 'low-capital' food-truck opening ignores the mandatory commissary and permit stack
edge_cases.trigger: a truck concept is treated as cheap entry on capital alone
edge_cases.mitigation: include the $900 city + county + $114 license + commissary stack as the binding entry constraint

edge_cases.description: Mariscos is read as a growth lane because it is culturally vibrant
edge_cases.trigger: local cultural durability is conflated with national segment growth
edge_cases.mitigation: classify mariscos as count-saturated, margin-fragile, but culturally durable — mature, not a growth lane

edge_cases.description: A festa- or summer-concentrated business is sized on a flat annual band
edge_cases.trigger: an annual revenue band is used for cash-flow planning without the seasonal profile
edge_cases.mitigation: overlay the format's peak profile (festas, Lent, summer, Muertos/Reyes) on the annual band before any working-capital read

edge_cases.description: Term-time student traffic is projected as year-round baseline demand
edge_cases.trigger: peak-semester café or fast-casual volume is annualized
edge_cases.mitigation: discount student-driven demand for the summer/break academic-calendar dip

edge_cases.description: Turlock's count is read as a deficit by comparing raw independent numbers to larger Modesto
edge_cases.trigger: absolute independent counts are compared without normalizing per capita
edge_cases.mitigation: normalize to independents-per-1,000 and read the ~20-30% locally owned share as healthy, not deficient

edge_cases.description: A secondary-category straddle inflates a format's apparent saturation count
edge_cases.trigger: a business counted under two formats (e.g., café + bakery) is tallied twice
edge_cases.mitigation: use primary category as the spine and note where secondaries justify a higher-end count without changing the saturation read

edge_cases.description: The 2026 Sysco/Restaurant Depot consolidation shifts small-operator input pricing mid-snapshot
edge_cases.trigger: a cash-and-carry pricing change moves the cost assumptions behind the bands
edge_cases.mitigation: treat the consolidation as a review-loop trigger and re-pair revenue bands with refreshed cost reality

edge_cases.description: CDTFA sales-tax receipts arrive and contradict the estimated pool and capture share
edge_cases.mitigation: fire the review loop, replace the pool/capture/distribution estimates with the measured figures, and re-derive the per-business read

workflow.description: Record the resident base, CSU enrollment, and ag/processing workforce with cited magnitudes
workflow.gate: three demand drivers each have a public-fact magnitude and a source confidence

workflow.description: Tie each heritage community and the student segment to the formats and dayparts they anchor
workflow.gate: each of the four communities and the student segment is tied to anchored formats with cited shares

workflow.description: Derive ~$99M as households x BLS spend, with range, confidence, and the CDTFA confirmation path
workflow.gate: the pool is stated as an estimate-not-actual with derivation, range, and confirmation path

workflow.action: Estimate independent capture and flag it
workflow.description: State the $35M-$50M low-confidence band and the outlet-vs-dollar-share tension
workflow.gate: the capture band is low-confidence-flagged with the downside scenario and CDTFA confirmation

workflow.description: Derive each format band as benchmark x size signal, paired with its cost/margin caveat
workflow.gate: every band is estimate-not-actual with a size signal, confidence, and cost/margin pairing

workflow.description: Show the ~$1M average is a pool mean and give the $300k-$700k typical cluster
workflow.gate: the average is labeled a pool mean and the typical-business band is stated as primary

workflow.action: Read the saturation equilibrium and per-format ceilings
workflow.description: Set each format's catalog count against its realistic ceiling and a saturated/balanced/room read
workflow.gate: each major format has a count, ceiling range, and saturation read consistent with the four forces

workflow.description: Classify formats as growing, mature, or declining and attach seasonal peaks
workflow.gate: growing/mature/declining formats are named with national-trend basis and seasonal peaks are flagged

workflow.action: Rank white-space and apply the cost gate
workflow.description: Order the defensible openings and mark each viable only after its cost gate clears
workflow.gate: five+ openings are ranked, each with a demand basis and a cost-gate qualifier

workflow.description: Compare per-capita density and structural format mix against Modesto, Merced, Manteca, Tracy, Ceres
workflow.gate: peer populations are cited, per-capita density is derived, and three+ peers are contrasted structurally

workflow.description: Combine saturation, white-space, trajectory, and cost gate into an add/avoid call
workflow.gate: the verdict refuses any demand-true but cost-gated addition and names the do-not-add formats

workflow.action: Set the market review cadence and triggers
workflow.description: Define the refresh cadence and material-change triggers routing back to pool sizing and saturation
workflow.gate: a cadence and a trigger list (CDTFA highest-leverage) routing to FOODAWAY_POOL and saturation exist

priority_rationale: Demand drivers, heritage and student demand are foundational because pool sizing, saturation, and white-space all read from them; pool sizing and capture precede the per-format bands and the pool-mean correction they constrain; saturation, growth/decline and white-space build on the demand and band layers; peer comparison and the ethnic over-index contextualize the saturation reads; the revenue-honesty guardrail governs every dollar expression; and the go/no-go verdict plus the review loop come last because they compose all upstream reads into a decision and a self-correcting refresh.

dominance_rules.rule: The revenue-honesty guardrail dominates any pressure for a single decisive number
dominance_rules.rationale: no per-business revenue is public, so an over-decisive figure would be a fabrication
dominance_rules.trigger: a request for a named business's revenue or a single market number
dominance_rules.action: answer only with a labeled estimate (benchmark x size signal) plus confidence and confirmation path

dominance_rules.rule: The cost gate dominates a demand-true white-space opening
dominance_rules.rationale: permitting and liquor-license cost can make a high-demand format un-enterable
dominance_rules.trigger: a white-space opening is judged attractive on demand alone
dominance_rules.action: mark it a no-go until the county-permit (and Type 47 for bar concepts) cost gate clears

dominance_rules.rule: The per-format typical band dominates the pool-mean average
dominance_rules.rationale: the ~$1M mean is tail-driven and not a typical business
dominance_rules.trigger: the per-business average is used to characterize a typical operator
dominance_rules.action: replace it with the $300k-$700k typical-independent band and label the mean low-confidence

dominance_rules.rule: Heritage durability dominates national-trend decline for heritage-anchored formats
dominance_rules.rationale: national casual-dining or coffee decline does not describe durable community-anchored formats
dominance_rules.trigger: a national decline signal is applied to a heritage format
dominance_rules.action: discount the national trend for formats with durable heritage demand

dominance_rules.rule: The Modesto ceiling dominates demand math for destination/fine-dining formats
dominance_rules.rationale: cross-shopping leaks destination demand to the larger neighbor regardless of local demand math
dominance_rules.trigger: a fourth fine-dining room is justified on Turlock demand alone
dominance_rules.action: cap the destination format at its ceiling and decline the addition

dominance_rules.rule: The seasonal profile dominates the annual band for cash-flow reads
dominance_rules.rationale: a flat annual band hides the festa/summer/Lent peaks that drive working-capital risk
dominance_rules.trigger: an annual band is used for a cash-flow or working-capital decision
dominance_rules.action: overlay the format's seasonal peak profile before deciding

dominance_rules.rule: Per-capita normalization dominates raw-count peer comparison
dominance_rules.rationale: comparing absolute independent counts across differently sized cities misleads
dominance_rules.trigger: Turlock's count is compared to a peer without normalizing per capita
dominance_rules.action: convert to independents-per-1,000 before drawing a saturation conclusion

dominance_rules.rule: A flagged low-confidence input dominates a confident downstream conclusion built on it
dominance_rules.rationale: a conclusion cannot be more certain than its weakest load-bearing input
dominance_rules.trigger: the capture share or a benchmark band carries a conclusion above its own confidence
dominance_rules.action: cap the conclusion's confidence at that of its weakest input and name the confirmation source

anti_rework_rules.rule: Size the resident pool before estimating independent capture or per-format bands
anti_rework_rules.prevents: deriving capture and bands against a pool that later moves, forcing a full re-derivation

anti_rework_rules.rule: Label every dollar figure estimate-not-actual at the moment it is written
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a later honesty sweep that must re-caveat figures already quoted as facts

anti_rework_rules.rule: Read saturation off primary category, noting secondary straddles, before counting
anti_rework_rules.prevents: double-counted straddle formats inflating a saturation read that must be re-tallied

anti_rework_rules.rule: Apply the cost gate while ranking white-space, not after recommending it
anti_rework_rules.prevents: recommending a bar-forward or mobile opening that the Type 47 or commissary gate then voids

anti_rework_rules.rule: Normalize peer comparison per capita before contrasting format mix
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a raw-count peer conclusion that must be redone once density is normalized

anti_rework_rules.rule: Attach the seasonal profile to a format's band when the band is built
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a flat-band cash-flow plan that must be reworked once the peaks are surfaced

anti_rework_rules.rule: Flag the capture share low-confidence and carry the downside the first time it is used
anti_rework_rules.prevents: every downstream market size inheriting an unflagged assumption that must be re-marked

anti_rework_rules.rule: Name the CDTFA confirmation path on every low-confidence dollar figure as it is stated
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a later pass to attach confirmation sources to numbers already published without them

iteration_protocol.trigger: CDTFA / Turlock Finance restaurants-and-hotels sales-tax receipts become available
iteration_protocol.action: replace the pool, capture share, and per-business distribution estimates with measured figures and re-derive the bands

iteration_protocol.trigger: a census/ACS demographic or CSU enrollment refresh lands
iteration_protocol.action: re-run the demand drivers and heritage/student demand and re-size the pool

iteration_protocol.trigger: a major local plant or distribution center opens or closes
iteration_protocol.action: update the ag/processing demand driver and re-read the affected saturation and white-space

iteration_protocol.trigger: a national restaurant-trend release updates growth/decline signals
iteration_protocol.action: refresh the trajectory overlay and re-rank white-space accordingly

iteration_protocol.trigger: a city/county/ABC permit or license fee or availability changes
iteration_protocol.action: re-price the cost gate and re-issue any affected go/no-go verdicts

iteration_protocol.trigger: a format opens or closes in the catalog
iteration_protocol.action: re-tally the saturation reads and the peer-city format-mix contrast

iteration_protocol.trigger: a peer-city population or foodservice-mix figure is refreshed
iteration_protocol.action: re-derive per-capita density and the ethnic over-index read

iteration_protocol.trigger: the Sysco/Restaurant Depot consolidation moves cash-and-carry input pricing
iteration_protocol.action: re-pair the revenue bands with refreshed cost reality and note the margin effect
